{{Short description|Type of logical fallacy}}
An '''appeal to the [[law]]''' ('''''argumentum ad legem''''' in Latin) is an informal [[fallacy]] in which someone tries to encourage or defend an action based on its legality, or condemn it as morally reprehensible, purely because it is [[Violation of law|illegal]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-22 |title='Well, It's Not Illegal!' {{!}} University of Central Florida News |url=https://www.ucf.edu/news/well-not-illegal/ |access-date=2022-06-07 |website=University of Central Florida News {{!}} UCF Today |language=en-us |archive-date=2022-03-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324054355/https://www.ucf.edu/news/well-not-illegal/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This line of reasoning is faulty because although the law of the land is important, it does not necessarily match up with the [[morality]] or [[Common sense|sensibility]] of an action.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Appeal to the Law |url=https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Appeal-to-the-Law |access-date=2022-06-07 |website=www.logicallyfallacious.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-21 |title=Appeal to Legality: Is it Moral if it's the Law? |url=https://cerebralistic.com/appeal-to-legality/ |access-date=2022-06-07 |website=Cerebralistic |language=en-US |archive-date=2021-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304171137/https://cerebralistic.com/appeal-to-legality/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ethics and Law |url=https://www.qcc.cuny.edu/socialsciences/ppecorino/ethics_text/chapter_1_introduction/Ethics_and_Law.htm#:~:text=Things%20that%20are%20illegal%20but,Smoking%20marijuana. |access-date=2022-06-07 |website=www.qcc.cuny.edu |archive-date=2021-11-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128023622/https://www.qcc.cuny.edu/socialsciences/ppecorino/ethics_text/chapter_1_introduction/Ethics_and_Law.htm#:~:text=Things%20that%20are%20illegal%20but,Smoking%20marijuana. |url-status=live }}</ref> In reality, many statutorily forbidden acts are ''[[malum prohibitum]]'' rather than ''[[malum in se]]''.

== Examples ==

* "So what if I cheated on my husband? It's not like being unfaithful is a crime!"
* "Filling your shoes with river water is cheap, simple ''and'' legal in all 50 states."
* "I think that routine circumcision is unethical, but my friend keeps arguing that because it's legal it must be ethical"
